topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its core learning objectives regarding cancer treatment approaches.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic drugs, alongside systemic toxicity and efflux pump-mediated resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell vulnerabilities, checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic biological vulnerabilities of cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine small-molecule therapies directed against hyperactivated oncogenic kinases, exploring oncogene addiction as well as structural and pathway mechanisms of acquired resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and cancer immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address strategies that harness the immune system to treat cancer, spanning monoclonal antibodies, immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Broader challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review systemic challenges in therapy development, historical progress in cancer survival and prevention, and emerging paradigms and dilemmas in clinical management.
